Source: Geological Survey of Pakistan / USGS COALREAP borehole analyses of the Thar coalfield, as compiled in the published proximate-analysis literature (n=54 as-received samples)
Note: THE REASON THIS SECTOR'S SO2 IS A BOUND RATHER THAN AN ESTIMATE. AP-42 Section 1.7 does not publish a lignite SO2 factor at all: Table 1.7-1 publishes 30S (22S for high-sodium ash, 34S for low-sodium; ash sodium is not held here, so the table's own 30S default is carried), where S is the sulfur weight percent of the lignite actually burned. NEPRA publishes no fuel analysis, so S comes from the coal literature, and the published Thar range spans a factor of eleven. Central value is the geometric mean of the range, uncertainty is derived from it, exactly as the fugitives sector handles IPCC's published factor ranges. These rows describe THAR LIGNITE by construction - the AP-42 rank split points the lignite share of coal energy here.

Source: Thar coalfield proximate analyses: 6.42 percent mean (one compilation) and 6.83 percent arithmetic mean (as-received, n=54)
Note: Ash drives the PM factors, which AP-42 Table 1.7-4 publishes as 6.5A filterable (tangential) with Table 1.7-7's cumulative distribution supplying 2.3A at 10 microns and 0.66A at 2.5. The two published means are close, so ash contributes far less spread than sulfur does. Thar lignite is a low-ash coal by world standards.
